questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. It is very hard for her to provide the necessities of her family .
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
It is very hard for her to provide the necessities of her family.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 1.
 
Key Points
  • The primary issue in the sentence is the choice of the preposition "of" after the term "necessities."
  • The preposition "to" is more appropriate to indicate the direction of providing something to someone.
  • The correct phrase should be "the necessities to her family", ensuring grammatical correctness and clarity.
  • Thus, the error is located in the underlined segment of the sentence.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.
 
Correct Sentence: "It is very hard for her to provide the necessities to her family."
 
Additional Information
  • Option 2: "the necessities by her family" – This implies the family provides the necessities, which is incorrect in this context.
  • Option 3: "the necessity of her family" – This changes the meaning to a single necessity, which is not the intended meaning.
  • Option 4: "the necessities from her families" – The plural form "families" and the preposition "from" are incorrect in this context.

questions.question: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. He will give a lecture on personality development.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.
He will give a lecture on personality development.

options.text: A lecture on personality development can be given by him.
options.html: A lecture on personality development can be given by him.

options.text: A lecture will be given on personality development.
options.html: A lecture will be given on personality development.

options.text: A lecture on personality development will be given by him.
options.html: A lecture on personality development will be given by him.

options.text: A lecture on personality development will be giving by him.
options.html: A lecture on personality development will be giving by him.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 3.
 
Key Points
  • Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.
  • In the active voice, the sentence is: "He will give a lecture on personality development."
  • To convert to passive voice: Place the object "a lecture on personality development" at the beginning.
  • Change the active verb form "will give" to "will be given" (future simple passive).
  • Add the preposition "by" followed by the original subject "him."
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.
 
Correct Sentence: "A lecture on personality development will be given by him."
 
Additional Information
  • Option 1: "A lecture on personality development can be given by him." – Incorrect modality (can instead of will).
  • Option 2: "A lecture will be given on personality development." – Incorrect structure, missing the agent (by him).
  • Option 4: "A lecture on personality development will be giving by him." – Incorrect verb form (giving instead of given).

questions.question: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. Note: This is an advertisement of an ice-cream brand. (A) That's why Silky is deliciously different and exceptionally versatile, natural, thick and durable ice cream. (B) Beautifully firm, nice, silky rather than thin and watery, it stays in shape and stands on top of fruits or pastries without soaking in. (C) Silky thick double ice cream has a unique, fresh taste and texture.
questions.questionHtml:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. Note: This is an advertisement of an ice-cream brand.
(A) That's why Silky is deliciously different and exceptionally versatile, natural, thick and durable ice cream.
(B) Beautifully firm, nice, silky rather than thin and watery, it stays in shape and stands on top of fruits or pastries without soaking in.
(C) Silky thick double ice cream has a unique, fresh taste and texture.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 3.
 
Key Points
  • The paragraph begins by introducing the unique qualities of the ice cream.
  • Sentence C is the first sentence as it sets the introduction:
    • "Silky thick double ice cream has a unique, fresh taste and texture."
  • Sentence B follows as it describes the specific characteristics of the ice cream:
    • "Beautifully firm, nice, silky rather than thin and watery, it stays in shape and stands on top of fruits or pastries without soaking in."
  • Sentence A is the third sentence as it concludes with why the ice cream is different:
    • "That's why Silky is deliciously different and exceptionally versatile, natural, thick and durable ice cream."
  • The correct sequence is CBA.
 
Coherent paragraph after rearrangement:
"Silky thick double ice cream has a unique, fresh taste and texture. Beautifully firm, nice, silky rather than thin and watery, it stays in shape and stands on top of fruits or pastries without soaking in. That's why Silky is deliciously different and exceptionally versatile, natural, thick and durable ice cream."

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Bully

Bully

The correct answer is: Oppressor.

Key Points

  • The word "bully" refers to a person who habitually seeks to harm or intimidate those whom they perceive as vulnerable. (धौंस जमाने वाला)
    • Example: He stood up to the bully who had been tormenting his friend.
  • "Oppressor" is someone who keeps others down by the cruel use of power. (अत्याचारी)
    • Example: The dictator was seen as an oppressor by the people of his country.
  • Hence, we can infer that a synonym for 'bully' is 'oppressor'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Oppressor.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Plough (हल): A large farming implement with one or more blades fixed in a frame, used to turn over and cut through the soil to prepare it for planting.
    • Example: The farmer used a plough to prepare the field for the new crop.
  • Oxen (बैल): Domesticated bovine animals used for pulling heavy loads.
    • Example: The oxen were yoked to the cart to transport the goods.
  • Coddle (लाड़ प्यार करना): Treat in an indulgent or overprotective way.
    • Example: She used to coddle her younger brother, much to his annoyance.

questions.question: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error. Dr. Sinha has / brought about a new / book on social / impact of child labour.
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.

Dr. Sinha has / brought about a new / book on social / impact of child labour.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 3.
 
Key Points​

The segment that contains an error is:

  1. "brought about a new"

Explanation:

  • The phrase "brought about" is incorrect in this context. "Brought about" means to cause or to make happen, which doesn't logically apply to the action of writing a book.
  • The correct phrase should be "brought out," which means to publish or release.

Corrected sentence: "Dr. Sinha has brought out a new book on the social impact of child labour."

Additional Information 

let's break down the sentence and explain why there is an error in segment 3:

Original sentence: "Dr. Sinha has / brought about a new / book on social / impact of child labour."

Segment-by-segment analysis:

  1. "Dr. Sinha has" - This segment is grammatically correct.
  2. "brought about a new" - This segment contains the error.
  3. "book on social" - This segment is grammatically correct.
  4. "impact of child labour" - This segment is grammatically correct.

Identifying the error in segment 3: "brought about a new"

Explanation:

  • "Brought about" means to cause something to happen. For example, "The new policy brought about significant changes."
  • In the context of publishing or releasing a book, the correct phrase should be "brought out," which means to publish or release. For example, "The author has brought out a new book."

Correct usage:

  • The correct phrase to use when referring to the publication of a book is "brought out."

Corrected sentence: "Dr. Sinha has brought out a new book on the social impact of child labour."

The correct segments are:

  1. "Dr. Sinha has"
  2. "brought out a new"
  3. "book on social"
  4. "impact of child labour"

So, the segment that contains the error is:

  1. "brought about a new"

It should be corrected to "brought out a new."

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. To the general public, William was best known as a crusader for peace and as an admired critic about social, political and ethical subjects.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
To the general public, William was best known as a crusader for peace and as an admired critic about social, political and ethical subjects.

options.text: for peace and as an admired critic by
options.html: for peace and as an admired critic by

options.text: for peace and as an admired critic on
options.html: for peace and as an admired critic on

options.text: about peace and as an admired critic about
options.html: about peace and as an admired critic about

options.text: in peace and as an admired critic about
options.html: in peace and as an admired critic about

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 2.
 
 Key Points​

Original sentence: "To the general public, William was best known as a crusader for peace and as an admired critic about social, political and ethical subjects."

  1. "for peace and as an admired critic on"
  • "on" is correct because it logically connects with "critic" to indicate the subjects (social, political, and ethical) that William critiques.

Thus, option 2 is the most appropriate because it maintains the parallel structure and clearly indicates what William is known for, both as a crusader for one cause (peace) and a critic on specific subjects (social, political, and ethical).

Correct Sentence: "To the general public, William was best known as a crusader for peace and as an admired critic on social, political and ethical subjects."
 
Additional Information
  1. "for peace and as an admired critic by"
  • "by" is incorrect because it suggests who admires the critic rather than what the critic is admiring or critiquing.
  1. "about peace and as an admired critic about"
  • Repeating "about" makes the sentence redundant and awkward. Moreover, "about peace" changes the meaning, implying "critic about peace," which doesn't fit the intended message.
  1. "in peace and as an admired critic about"

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom. In those days, we did not expect luxuries; we were thankful if we could keep the wolf from the door .
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom.

In those days, we did not expect luxuries; we were thankful if we could keep the wolf from the door.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 1.

Key Points

  • The idiom "keep the wolf from the door" means to avoid starvation or financial ruin; it implies managing to survive with the basic necessities. (भुखमरी से बचना)
    • Example: During the recession, many families struggled to keep the wolf from the door.
  • "Avoid starvation" means ensuring that one has enough food to survive, preventing hunger. (भुखमरी से बचना)
    • Example: They worked hard to avoid starvation during the drought.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Avoid starvation.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Wallow in poverty (गरीबी में डूबना): To live in a state of extreme poverty and make no effort to improve the situation.
    • Example: Instead of wallowing in poverty, they sought ways to improve their living conditions.
  • Relish food (भोजन का आनंद लेना): To enjoy or take pleasure in eating food.
    • Example: He relished the food served at the grand banquet.
  • Encourage starvation (भुखमरी को प्रोत्साहित करना): To support or promote a state of not having enough food to eat.
    • Example: Their cruel policies seemed to encourage starvation among the poor.

The correct answer is 'regardless'.
 
Key Points
  • The word "regardless" means "despite or although" and is used to introduce a statement that contrasts with or seems to contradict something that has just been said. (के बावजूद)
  • Example: Regardless of the heavy rain, the event continued as planned.
  • In the given sentence, the phrase "regardless of what may or may not be true of my personal scholastic rigour" aligns with the context, emphasizing a contrast with the earlier statement. (व्यक्तिगत शैक्षणिक कड़ी मेहनत के बारे में जो सच हो सकता है या नहीं हो सकता है, इसके बावजूद।)
Therefore, the correct answer is 'regardless'.
 
Additional Information
  • Nevertheless (फिर भी): Indicates "in spite of that" or "however." It introduces a contrast but does not fit the context of contrasting a hypothetical situation. Example: The weather was cold; nevertheless, we went hiking.
  • Notwithstanding (इसके बावजूद): Means "without paying attention to the current circumstances." It doesn’t carry the precise sense of introducing a conditional contrast. Example: He continued his studies notwithstanding of financial difficulties.
  • Inasmuch (इस हद तक कि): Means "to the extent that" or "because." It is used to show a cause or condition rather than a contrast. Example: He should be held responsible inasmuch as he was aware of the rules.
